text:
anya: FYI I hit a nasty flake in the Java/Kotlin SDK when running the Android sample app on API 21. App stalls on long requests and then crashes with IllegalStateException from OkHttp
kevin: ugh, stack?
sam: have you tried bumping okhttp? Android minimums sometimes interact weirdly with timeouts
anya: stack trace snippet:
```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: callAlreadyExecuted
	at okhttp3.RealCall.execute(RealCall.java:??)
	at com.redwood.sdk.transport.OkHttpTransport.execute(OkHttpTransport.kt:45)
```
anya: Root cause seems to be our transport reusing Call instances across retries + using `call.timeout()` in retry path. On Android a cancelled call sometimes leaves internal state that trips the second execute.
android-eng: also saw issues where `call.timeout()` is no-op on older okhttp/android combos and you still rely on `readTimeout`/`writeTimeout`
kevin: we intentionally used call.timeout for per-request timeouts because Retrofit's client-level timeouts were too coarse. But OK. What's the failure scenario?
anya: sequence: request -> transient 503 -> retry interceptor clones call but reuses same Call object -> second execute -> IllegalStateException. Also observed that on emulators the timing was different vs real devices (real devices more likely to hit the race).
sam: interceptors order matters. If our RetryInterceptor is installed before the Authenticator or before the header-interceptor that injects API key, the retried call might miss updated headers (token refresh race).
kevin: aha. We also got a report of 401 on retry because the token was refreshed asynchronously by Authenticator but our retry clones didn't pick it up.
anya: exact repro in sample app:
1) network returns 401 with body A
2) Authenticator triggers token refresh (background)
3) RetryInterceptor retries immediately using stale headers -> 401 again -> gives up
4) App-side sees failed auth, then SDK triggers another refresh but it's noisy

I patched locally to: (a) create a fresh Request for each retry using client.newCall(request) rather than reusing Call, (b) move RetryInterceptor to be after the Authenticator/headers injector, and (c) avoid call.timeout manipulation on Android < 23 and fallback to per-client readTimeout as a conservative choice.
kevin: can you paste the code change for the OkHttp builder?
anya: sure:```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .addInterceptor(HeaderInjectorInterceptor()) // ensure headers applied before retries
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor())
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // default to 0, per-request timeouts handled carefully
  .build()
// inside RetryInterceptor we now do:
// val newCall = chain.call().client().newCall(request)
```
sam: small note: `chain.call().client()` is internal; prefer storing the OkHttpClient instance in the interceptor constructor so you can call client.newCall(request). Also ensure `retryOnConnectionFailure` true for transient network errors.
android-eng: we should also add an Android compatibility matrix in the repo README listing tested okhttp+retrofit combos and the workaround matrix for call.timeout vs readTimeout. 
kevin: agreed. Also add a unit/instrumented test: simulate 401 then successful token refresh and ensure the retry obtains refreshed credentials. Use MockWebServer to orchestrate responses.
anya: I added a quick MockWebServer test locally. It failed initially because our sample app's Application singleton reuses a single OkHttpClient where our test expected a new client per test run. Switched to TestHarness that constructs fresh client per test.
ci-bot: build #4821 started for PR #920 (anya/okhttp-retries)
kevin: can we also turn down dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost when running on low-end devices? We saw thread pool starvation on older devices causing huge tail latencies
sam: good call. Setting dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost to something like 6 for mobile might help. Add config option on the SDK to tune dispatcher in Android builder.
android-eng: another gotcha: okhttp 5 changed package names; don't bump to 5 in mobile SDK until we have full integration tests + proguard/R8 rules updated.
anya: next steps:
- I will open PR with the client config changes + RetryInterceptor tweaks + MockWebServer test (WIP).
- kevin can add documented compatibility matrix to /samples/android/README.md
- sam will add a small instrumented test to run on CI emulator suite to catch regresses on API 21/23/30
kevin: assigned. Also add a short blurb in dx-notes channel for onboarding so sample app doesn't mislead devs into copying the problematic pattern.
anya: thanks all. Will push PR when CI passes. :thumbsup:
